   634→
   635→## CLI Interface (kspec)
   636→
   637→### Design Philosophy
   638→
   639→Following the **git plumbing/porcelain model**:
   640→
   641→- **Plumbing**: Low-level atomic primitives for scripts and agents
   642→- **Porcelain**: High-level convenient commands for humans
   643→
   644→### Command Structure
   645→
   646→```
   647→kspec <resource> <action> [args] [flags]
   648→```
   649→
   650→### Core Commands
   651→
   652→#### Item Operations
   653→
   654→```bash
   655→# Create
   656→kspec item add --type feature --title "User Login" --id auth-login
   657→
   658→# Read
   659→kspec item get auth-login
   660→kspec item get auth-login --field status
   661→kspec item list --type feature --status pending
   662→
   663→# Update
   664→kspec item set auth-login --field status.maturity --value stable
   665→kspec item patch auth-login --data '{"priority": "high"}'
   666→
   667→# Delete
   668→kspec item delete auth-login --force
   669→```
   670→
   671→#### Link Operations
   672→
   673→```bash
   674→# Create relationship
   675→kspec link create auth-login auth-session --type depends_on
   676→
   677→# Query relationships
   678→kspec link list --from auth-login
   679→kspec link graph --from auth-login --depth 3
   680→
   681→# Remove relationship
   682→kspec link delete auth-login auth-session
   683→```
   684→
   685→#### Query Operations
   686→
   687→```bash
   688→# Structured queries
   689→kspec item list --type feature --status pending --has-tag mvp
   690→
   691→# Complex queries (jq-style)
   692→kspec query '.items[] | select(.priority == "high") | .id'
   693→
   694→# Aggregation
   695→kspec count --type feature --group-by status
   696→```
   697→
   698→#### Validation
   699→
   700→```bash
   701→# Full validation
   702→kspec validate
   703→
   704→# Specific checks
   705→kspec validate --schema      # Schema conformance
   706→kspec validate --refs        # All references resolve
   707→kspec validate --orphans     # Find unreferenced items
   708→
   709→# In CI
   710→kspec lint --strict
   711→```
   712→
   713→#### Diff and History
   714→
   715→```bash
   716→kspec diff --since HEAD~1
   717→kspec diff --since spec-v1.0.0
   718→kspec history auth-login
   719→```
   720→
   721→### Agent-Friendly Features
   722→
   723→| Feature | Implementation |
   724→|---------|----------------|
   725→| **JSON output** | `--json` or `--output json` on all commands |
   726→| **Idempotency** | `--if-not-exists`, `--if-changed` flags |
   727→| **Non-interactive** | `--no-prompt` flag, `KSPEC_NO_PROMPT=1` env |
   728→| **Dry-run** | `--dry-run` shows what would change |
   729→| **Clear errors** | Structured JSON errors with codes and suggestions |
   730→| **Semantic exit codes** | 0=success, 3=not found, 4=validation failed, etc. |
   731→
   732→### Example Session
   733→
   734→```bash
   735→# Agent creates a new feature
   736→$ kspec item add --type feature --id user-export \
   737→    --title "Data Export" \
   738→    --field "description=Allow users to export their data" \
   739→    --json
   740→{
   741→  "success": true,
   742→  "item": {"id": "user-export", "title": "Data Export", ...}
   743→}
   744→
   745→# Agent adds a dependency
   746→$ kspec link create user-export user-model --type depends_on --json
   747→{
   748→  "success": true,
   749→  "link": {"from": "user-export", "to": "user-model", "type": "depends_on"}
   750→}
   751→
   752→# Validate before commit
   753→$ kspec validate --json
   754→{
   755→  "valid": true,
   756→  "warnings": [],
   757→  "errors": []
   758→}
   759→```
   760→
   761→---
   762→
   763→## Traceability
   764→
   765→### Tiered Approach
   766→
   767→Traceability is **opt-in and progressive** based on project needs:
   768→
   769→#### Tier 1: Implicit (Default)
   770→
   771→- No explicit links between spec and code
   772→- Rely on naming conventions and structure
   773→- Spec: `spec/auth/login.yaml` → Code: `src/auth/login.ts`
   774→- Zero overhead
   775→
   776→#### Tier 2: Convention-Based
   777→
   778→- Stable IDs enable tracing
   779→- Commit message convention: `Implements: auth-login`
   780→- Test tagging: `@pytest.mark.spec("auth-login")`
   781→- Optional: Generate traceability reports
   782→
   783→```yaml
   784→# Conventional commits
   785→feat(auth): implement login endpoint
   786→
   787→Implements: auth-login
   788→Refs: #42
   789→```
   790→
   791→#### Tier 3: Formal Bidirectional
   792→
   793→- Full traceability required (regulated industries)
   794→- Spec items link to code locations
   795→- Code annotations link back to spec
   796→- CI validation enforces completeness
   797→
   798→```yaml
   799→# In spec
   800→traceability:
   801→  implementation:
   802→    - path: src/auth/login.ts
   803→      function: handleLogin
   804→      lines: 45-78
   805→  tests:
   806→    - path: tests/auth/login.test.ts
   807→  commits: [abc123]
   808→```
   809→
   810→```typescript
   811→// In code
   812→// @implements auth-login
   813→export async function handleLogin(credentials: Credentials) {
   814→  // ...
   815→}
   816→```
   817→
   818→### Recommendation
   819→
   820→**Start at Tier 1**, evolve to Tier 2 as specs stabilize, use Tier 3 only when compliance requires it. The format supports all tiers; the tooling makes each tier easy.
   821→
   822→---
   823→
   824→## Architecture
   825→
   826→### Design Philosophy: Unix-Style Primitives
   827→
   828→Kynetic Spec follows the **Unix philosophy**: do one thing well, compose with other tools.
   829→
   830→Instead of a plugin architecture where plugins integrate INTO kspec:
   831→```
   832→kspec → [plugin system] → outputs  ❌
   833→```
   834→
   835→Kspec is a **clean primitive** that other tools consume:
   836→```
   837→kspec (library/CLI) → JSON/structured output → any tool  ✅
   838→```
   839→
   840→### Library-First Design
   841→
   842→The core is a **TypeScript library** that can be consumed by:
   843→- The `kspec` CLI (primary interface)
   844→- Kynetic project integration
   845→- Custom tooling
   846→- CI/CD pipelines
   847→
   848→```typescript
   849→import { KyneticSpec, Item } from '@kynetic/spec';
   850→
   851→const spec = await KyneticSpec.load('./spec');
   852→const features = spec.items.filter(i => i.type === 'feature');
   853→const json = spec.toJSON();
   854→```
   855→
   856→### Schema Definition: Zod
   857→
   858→Schema is defined using **Zod** (TypeScript-native validation library):
   859→
   860→```
   861→Zod schemas (source of truth)
   862→    ├── z.infer<> → TypeScript types (compile-time)
   863→    ├── z.toJSONSchema() → JSON Schema (for docs, external validation)
   864→    └── quicktype/agents → other language bindings (if needed)
   865→```
   866→
   867→**Why Zod**:
   868→- Largest ecosystem in TypeScript validation space
   869→- Native type inference (no separate type definitions)
   870→- JSON Schema export in v4
   871→- Excellent DX and framework integration
   872→
   873→### Consuming Tools (Examples)
   874→
   875→Tools that might consume the kspec library/output:
   876→
   877→| Tool | Purpose | Integration |
   878→|------|---------|-------------|
   879→| `kspec-docs` | Generate markdown documentation | Library consumer |
   880→| `kspec-github` | Sync to GitHub Issues | Library consumer |
   881→| Kynetic | Task orchestration | Library integration |
   882→| CI pipelines | Validation, reports | CLI JSON output |
   883→
   884→Each tool is independent, maintained separately, and composes with kspec rather than being embedded in it.
   885→
   886→### Git Hooks
   887→
   888→Hooks are **declarative in config** + **opt-in installation**:
   889→
   890→```yaml
   891→# In spec manifest
   892→hooks:
   893→  commit-msg: validate-refs    # What hooks are wanted
   894→  pre-commit: lint
   895→```
   896→
   897→```bash
   898→# Developer opts in
   899→kspec hooks install    # Reads config, sets up hooks
   900→kspec hooks uninstall  # Removes hooks
   901→```
   902→
   903→CI can enforce the same checks without requiring hooks installed locally.
   904→
   905→---
   906→
   907→## Implementation Roadmap
   908→
   909→### Phase 1: Foundation
   910→
   911→- [ ] Finalize YAML schema and conventions
   912→- [ ] Create JSON Schema for validation
   913→- [ ] Implement core CLI (`kspec` command)
   914→  - [ ] `item add/get/list/set/delete`
   915→  - [ ] `validate`
   916→  - [ ] `--json` output mode
   917→- [ ] Basic documentation
   918→
   919→### Phase 2: Relationships and Queries
   920→
   921→- [ ] Implement `link` commands
   922→- [ ] Cross-reference validation
   923→- [ ] Query capabilities (filtering, graph traversal)
   924→- [ ] `diff` command for comparing versions
   925→
   926→### Phase 3: Agent Integration
   927→
   928→- [ ] Optimize for agent usage patterns
   929→- [ ] Add `--dry-run`, idempotent operations
   930→- [ ] Improve error messages for agent consumption
   931→- [ ] Create agent integration guide
   932→
   933→### Phase 4: Plugins and Outputs
   934→
   935→- [ ] Define plugin interface
   936→- [ ] Implement `markdown-docs` plugin
   937→- [ ] Implement `task-list` plugin
   938→- [ ] Plugin discovery and loading
   939→
   940→### Phase 5: Advanced Features
   941→
   942→- [ ] Traceability tooling (Tier 2 and 3)
   943→- [ ] GitHub/Linear issue sync plugins
   944→- [ ] Visual dependency graphs
   945→- [ ] Baseline comparison reports
   946→
   947→---
   948→
   949→## Resolved Decisions
   950→
   951→The following decisions were made through collaborative exploration:
   952→
   953→### Format and Structure
   954→
   955→| Decision | Resolution |
   956→|----------|------------|
   957→| **File structure** | **Auto-adaptive**: Start as single file, CLI offers to split when spec grows (threshold: ~500 lines or 20+ items) |
   958→| **ID system** | **ULID + Slugs**: ULID is canonical (shortenable like git hashes), slugs are agent-generated aliases |
   959→| **Schema layer** | **Zod**: TypeScript-native, exports JSON Schema, largest ecosystem |
   960→| **Runtime** | **TypeScript/Node**: Library-first design, CLI as one consumer |
   961→
   962→### Architecture
   963→
   964→| Decision | Resolution |
   965→|----------|------------|
   966→| **Plugin model** | **Inverted**: No plugin system. Kspec is a clean primitive; other tools consume it (Unix philosophy) |
   967→| **Library design** | **Library-first**: Core is a TS library; CLI and Kynetic integration consume it |
   968→| **Git hooks** | **Declarative config + opt-in install**: Manifest declares hooks, `kspec hooks install` sets them up |
   969→
   970→### Traceability and Workflow
   971→
   972→| Decision | Resolution |
   973→|----------|------------|
   974→| **Traceability** | **Opt-in enforcement**: Configurable in manifest, validated when enabled |
   975→| **Issue sync** | **One-way default**: Spec is authoritative; sync tools can add bidirectionality |
   976→| **Approval state** | **Optional metadata**: Fields exist but are optional; teams needing audit trails use them |
   977→
   978→### Multi-Repository and Templates
   979→
   980→| Decision | Resolution |
   981→|----------|------------|
   982→| **Multi-repo** | **Scaffold pattern**: One-time import, not live dependency. `kspec scaffold <url>` copies items |
   983→| **Templates** | **Dual support**: Regular specs can be scaffolded; optional template format with markers for dynamic generation |
   984→
   985→### Task System
   986→
   987→| Decision | Resolution |
   988→|----------|------------|
   989→| **Task-spec relationship** | **Hybrid with types**: Spec-derived tasks follow stricter rules; free-form tasks (infra, bugs) are looser |
   990→| **Data duplication** | **Reference, don't copy**: Tasks reference spec via `spec_ref`; don't duplicate spec content |
   991→| **Task storage** | **Auto-adaptive**: Start alongside specs, separate `tasks/` directory when volume grows |
   992→| **Task IDs** | **Same as specs**: ULID + slugs, unified ID system |
   993→| **Task states** | **Standard 5-state + derived**: pending, in_progress, blocked, completed, cancelled. Blocked auto-computed from deps |
   994→| **Concurrency** | **External constraint**: Kspec doesn't enforce WIP limits; orchestration layer handles that |
   995→| **Task derivation** | **Command-triggered**: `kspec derive @feature` when explicitly requested, not automatic |
   996→| **Notes/updates** | **Append-only with supersession**: Entries never deleted, but new entries can supersede old ones |
   997→| **Todos** | **Promote pattern**: Start as lightweight checklist items, promote to full subtasks when complex |
   998→| **VCS linking** | **Minimal + extensible**: Simple refs (branch/commit/tag), type optional, extend schema as needed |
   999→
  1000→### ID System Details
  1001→
  1002→**Canonical ID**: ULID (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier)
  1003→- Time-sortable
  1004→- Can be shortened like git hashes: `01HQ3K5X...` → `01HQ3K`
  1005→- Never changes, never reused
  1006→
  1007→**Slugs**: Human-friendly aliases
  1008→- Agent-generated based on content/context
  1009→- Multiple slugs can point to same ULID
  1010→- Can evolve over time
  1011→
  1012→**Reference syntax**:
  1013→```yaml
  1014→depends_on:
  1015→  - "@01HQ3K"        # Short ULID reference
  1016→  - "@auth-login"    # Slug reference (resolved to ULID)
  1017→```
  1018→
  1019→---
  1020→
  1021→## Appendices
  1022→
  1023→### A. Comparison with Alternatives
  1024→
  1025→See [FORMAT_COMPARISON.md](./FORMAT_COMPARISON.md) for detailed format comparison.
  1026→
  1027→### B. Research Sources
  1028→
  1029→The design was informed by research into:
  1030→- Requirements management tools (IBM DOORS, Jama Connect, ReqIF)
  1031→- Documentation-as-code tools (OpenAPI, Cucumber/Gherkin, ADRs)
  1032→- CLI design patterns (kubectl, gh, terraform)
  1033→- Versioning practices (SemVer, git tagging, RFC lifecycle)
  1034→- Traceability standards (DO-178C, IEC 62304, ISO 26262)
  1035→
  1036→### C. Glossary
  1037→
  1038→| Term | Definition |
  1039→|------|------------|
  1040→| **Item** | The fundamental unit in a spec (feature, requirement, etc.) |
  1041→| **UID** | Unique identifier for an item (stable, never reused) |
  1042→| **Baseline** | A named snapshot of the spec at a point in time |
  1043→| **Traceability** | Links between spec items and implementation artifacts |
  1044→| **Plumbing** | Low-level CLI commands for scripting |
  1045→| **Porcelain** | High-level CLI commands for humans |
  1046→
  1047→---
  1048→
  1049→*This document is itself a Kynetic Spec artifact, demonstrating the format it describes.*
  1050→

        given: command supports JSON mode
        when: --json flag is provided

        given: JSON mode is active
        when: command completes successfully

        given: JSON mode is active
        when: command encounters an error
        then: error is returned as JSON object with error field

        when: output is generated
        then: references use @ prefix consistently
      - id: ac-5
        given: JSON output contains timestamps
        when: output is generated

      - id: ac-7

_ulid: 01KF1XMETA0000000000000000
slugs:
  - meta
  - meta-spec
  - meta-module
title: Meta-Spec System
type: module
status:
  maturity: draft
  implementation: implemented
description: |
  Meta-spec is the layer that defines HOW work happens, separate from
  WHAT is being built (spec) and tracking WORK (tasks).

  The key distinction:
  - Spec: What to build (features, requirements)
  - Tasks: Work to do (implement feature X)
  - Meta-spec: How to work (check spec before implementing)

  Meta-spec enables a self-improvement loop:
  1. Define workflows → 2. Track adherence → 3. Identify friction →
  4. Propose improvements → 5. Update workflows → (repeat)

  Meta-spec complements prose docs (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md) rather than
  replacing them. Structured definitions + prose guidance work together.
features:
  - _ulid: 01KF1XMNF00000000000000000
    slugs:
      - meta-manifest
      - meta-file
    title: Meta Manifest
    type: feature
    status:
      maturity: draft
      implementation: implemented
    priority: high
    tags:
      - mvp
      - meta
    description: |
      The meta manifest (kynetic.meta.yaml) is the root file for process
      definitions. It lives alongside kynetic.yaml and defines agents,
      workflows, conventions, and observations.

      Unlike spec items which define product features, meta items define
      how work is done on the project.
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: ac-meta-manifest-1
        given: a project with kynetic.yaml
        when: kynetic.meta.yaml is created with valid structure
        then: >
          kspec meta show outputs summary with counts for agents, workflows, conventions, and
          observations (exit code 0)
      - id: ac-meta-manifest-2
        given: a meta manifest exists
        when: kspec validate runs
        then: >
          output includes "Meta: X agents, Y workflows, Z conventions" line; validation errors for
          meta items use "meta:" prefix to distinguish from spec errors
      - id: ac-meta-manifest-3
        given: kynetic.meta.yaml has invalid schema
        when: kspec validate runs
        then: >
          exits with code 1; error message identifies the invalid field path and expected type
          (e.g., "meta:agents[0].capabilities: expected array")
    requirements:
      - _ulid: 01KF1XMNF10000000000000000
        slugs:
          - meta-manifest-format
        title: Meta Manifest Format
        type: requirement
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: implemented
        description: |
          Meta manifest structure:

          ```yaml
          kynetic_meta: "1.0"

          agents:
            - _ulid: ...
              id: claude
              name: Claude Code Agent
              ...

          workflows:
            - _ulid: ...
              id: spec-first
              trigger: behavior change
              ...

          conventions:
            - _ulid: ...
              domain: commits
              ...

          observations:
            - _ulid: ...
              type: friction
              ...

          includes:
            - meta/agents.yaml
            - meta/workflows.yaml
          ```

          Version field enables schema evolution.
        implements:
          - "@meta-manifest"
      - _ulid: 01KF1XMNF20000000000000000
        slugs:
          - meta-includes
        title: Meta Includes
        type: requirement
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: implemented
        description: |
          Meta manifest supports includes for organization:

          ```yaml
          includes:
            - meta/agents.yaml
            - meta/workflows.yaml
            - meta/conventions.yaml
          ```

          Allows splitting large meta-specs into focused files.
          Same pattern as spec manifest includes.
        implements:
          - "@meta-manifest"
      - _ulid: 01KF1XMNF30000000000000000
        slugs:
          - meta-validation
        title: Meta Validation Integration
        type: requirement
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: implemented
        description: |
          `kspec validate` includes meta-spec validation:

          - Schema validation for all meta item types
          - Reference resolution (@refs in workflows, observations)
          - Cross-validation with product spec (meta-refs exist)

          Unified validation ensures consistency across both layers.
        implements:
          - "@meta-manifest"

<script lang="ts">
	import { onMount, onDestroy } from 'svelte';
	import { base } from '$app/paths';
	import type { PlanSummary } from '@kynetic-ai/shared';
	import { fetchPlans } from '$lib/api';
	import { isStaticMode } from '$lib/stores/mode.svelte';
	import { subscribe, unsubscribe, on, off } from '$lib/stores/connection.svelte';
	import { getProjectVersion } from '$lib/stores/project.svelte';
	import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader } from '$lib/components/ui/card';
	import { Badge } from '$lib/components/ui/badge';
	import { Button } from '$lib/components/ui/button';
	import MapIcon from '@lucide/svelte/icons/map';
	import FileTextIcon from '@lucide/svelte/icons/file-text';
	import ListTodoIcon from '@lucide/svelte/icons/list-todo';

	// ── Data state ──
	let plans = $state<PlanSummary[]>([]);
	let loading = $state(true);
	let error = $state('');

	// ── Filter state ──
	type PlanStatusFilter = 'all' | 'draft' | 'approved' | 'active' | 'completed' | 'rejected';
	let filterStatus = $state<PlanStatusFilter>('all');

	// ── Plan status labels and colors ──
	// AC: @ui-plans-view ac-1 — visually distinct statuses with text labels
	const PLAN_STATUS_LABELS: Record<string, string> = {
		draft: 'Draft',
		approved: 'Approved',
		active: 'Active',
		completed: 'Completed',
		rejected: 'Rejected'
	};

	const PLAN_STATUS_COLORS: Record<string, string> = {
		draft: 'bg-status-pending text-status-pending-fg',
		approved: 'bg-status-pending-review text-status-pending-review-fg',
		active: 'bg-status-in-progress text-status-in-progress-fg',
		completed: 'bg-status-completed text-status-completed-fg',
		rejected: 'bg-status-blocked text-status-blocked-fg'
	};

	// ── Filtered plans ──
	let filteredPlans = $derived.by(() => {
		if (filterStatus === 'all') return plans;
		return plans.filter((p) => p.status === filterStatus);
	});

	// ── Status summary counts ──
	let statusCounts = $derived.by(() => {
		const counts: Record<string, number> = {};
		for (const plan of plans) {
			counts[plan.status] = (counts[plan.status] ?? 0) + 1;
		}
		return counts;
	});

	// ── Lifecycle ──
	onMount(async () => {
		await loadData();

		if (!isStaticMode()) {
			// Plan progress is derived from task statuses, so subscribe to tasks:updates
			// to refresh when task status changes (e.g., task completed → plan progress updates)
			subscribe(['tasks:updates']);
			on('tasks:updates', handleUpdate);
		}
	});

	onDestroy(() => {
		if (!isStaticMode()) {
			off('tasks:updates', handleUpdate);
			unsubscribe(['tasks:updates']);
		}
	});

	// Reload on project change
	$effect(() => {
		const version = getProjectVersion();
		if (version > 0) {
			loadData();
		}
	});

	// ── Data loading ──
	async function loadData() {
		try {
			loading = true;
			error = '';
			const response = await fetchPlans();
			plans = response.items;
		} catch (err) {
			error = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to load plans';
		} finally {
			loading = false;
		}
	}

Perfect! Now I have comprehensive architectural context. Let me create a detailed summary document for you.

## UI Revamp Plan - Architectural Context for Workflows Page

Based on my thorough analysis of the codebase, here's the complete architectural context for implementing the workflows page in the web UI:

---

### OVERALL ARCHITECTURE

**Web UI Stack:**
- **Framework**: SvelteKit with Svelte 5 (runes-based reactivity)
- **UI Components**: shadcn-svelte (Radix UI Svelte wrappers)
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4 with design token system (oklch color tokens, spacing, radii)
- **State Management**: Svelte 5 runes ($state, $derived, $effect)
- **API Communication**: Daemon REST API + WebSocket for real-time updates
- **Deployment**: Elysia.js daemon server (Bun runtime) serving bundled SvelteKit static assets

**Deployment Modes:**
1. **Daemon mode** (primary): Long-running server with WebSocket real-time updates
2. **Static mode** (GitHub Pages): Read-only SPA using embedded JSON snapshot
3. **Multi-directory mode**: Single daemon supporting multiple kspec projects via X-Kspec-Dir header

---

### COMPONENT PATTERNS EXPECTED

**Standard Page Structure:**
1. Title + description heading (h1 + muted text)
2. Error state display (alert banner)
3. Loading skeleton (matching content layout)
4. Main content section with data
5. Empty state (when no items) with icon, message, and help text

**Data Loading Pattern:**
```typescript
// Svelte 5 runes pattern observed in agents, plans pages:
let data = $state([]);
let loading = $state(true);
let error = $state('');

onMount(() => {
  loadData();
  if (!isStaticMode()) {
    subscribe(['topic']);
    on('topic', handleUpdate);
  }
});

$effect(() => {
  const version = getProjectVersion();
  if (version > 0) loadData();  // Reload on project change
});

onDestroy(() => {
  if (!isStaticMode()) {
    off('topic', handleUpdate);
    unsubscribe(['topic']);
  }
});
```

**WebSocket Integration:**
- Subscribe to topics for live updates (files:updates, agents, tasks:updates, etc.)
- Graceful degradation in static mode (skip WebSocket, load static data)
- Exponential backoff reconnection with 30s max
- Sequence deduplication for duplicate event handling

**API Pattern:**
- Conditional routing: `if (isStaticMode()) { return fetchDataStatic(...) }`
- Auto-injects X-Kspec-Dir header for multi-project support
- Project version tracking triggers data reloads

**Status/Badge Styling (Design Tokens):**
```
Status color mapping:
- pending → bg-status-pending / text-status-pending-fg (amber)
- in_progress → bg-status-in-progress / text-status-in-progress-fg (orange)
- pending_review → bg-status-pending-review / text-status-pending-review-fg (blue)
- completed → bg-status-completed / text-status-completed-fg (emerald)
- blocked → bg-status-blocked / text-status-blocked-fg (red)
- needs_work → bg-status-needs-work / text-status-needs-work-fg (yellow)
- cancelled → bg-status-cancelled / text-status-cancelled-fg (gray)
```

---

### SPECIFIC MENTIONS OF WORKFLOWS PAGE

**Spec Reference:** `@ui-workflows-view` (Feature ID: 01KK2TDXAKM3A0HBWJ71APCM9Q)

**Acceptance Criteria (ac-1):**
> Given workflow definitions exist in meta  
> When the user navigates to /workflows  
> Then each workflow shows id, description, ordered steps with names, trigger type if configured, and loop variant indicator. A Start button initiates the workflow via daemon API.

**Navigation Integration:**
- Sidebar group: "Config" (alongside Settings)
- Icon: Workflow (from lucide-svelte)
- Route: `/workflows` (already exists as stub)

**Shared Types Available:**
```typescript
// From @kynetic-ai/shared/api.ts
export interface Workflow {
  _ulid: string;
  slugs: string[];
  name: string;
  steps: WorkflowStep[];
}

export interface WorkflowStep {
  _ulid: string;
  type: 'action' | 'check' | 'decision';
  content: string;
}
```

---

### DESIGN TOKENS AND STYLING APPROACH

**Color System (oklch-based):**
- Light theme: `oklch(...)` values defined in CSS custom properties
- Dark theme: Separate oklch values for dark mode (`.dark` class)
- Opacity support: `oklch(...  / 10%)` for transparent variants
- No hardcoded hex colors—all from design tokens

**Available Design Tokens:**
- **Colors**: 16 base tokens + status colors (pending, in_progress, pending_review, completed, blocked, needs_work, cancelled)
- **Radii**: sm/md/lg/xl (0.375rem – 0.875rem based on --radius)
- **Spacing**: All standard Tailwind utilities
- **Z-index**: Configured via theme
- **Typography**: Font families from design token system
- **Animations**: Shimmer (loading), pulse (active agents), gated behind `prefers-reduced-motion`

**Key Utility Classes:**
- Status badges: `bg-status-[status] text-status-[status]-fg`
- Muted text: `text-muted-foreground`
- Card backgrounds: `bg-card`
- Borders: `border border-border`
- Rounded: `rounded-lg` (uses --radius-lg)

**shadcn-svelte Components Used:**
- `Card`, `CardHeader`, `CardContent`, `CardFooter`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`
- `Badge`, `Button`, `Separator`
- `Skeleton` (for loading states)
- `Accordion` (for expandable sections)
- `Sidebar`, `SidebarMenu`, `SidebarMenuItem`, `SidebarMenuButton`, etc.

---

### NAVIGATION STRUCTURE

**App Shell (Sidebar + SidebarInset Layout):**
```
┌─ Sidebar ──────────────────────┐
│ Header (Project Selector)       │
├─ NavGroups ────────────────────┤
│ Work                           │
│ ├─ Dashboard                   │
│ ├─ Tasks (badge: pending_review)
│ ├─ Agents                      │
│ └─ Sessions                    │
│ Specs                          │
│ ├─ Specs                       │
│ ├─ Plans                       │
│ └─ Validate                    │
│ Capture                        │
│ ├─ Inbox (badge: count)        │
│ ├─ Observations (badge: count) │
│ └─ Triage                      │
│ Config                         │
│ ├─ Workflows  ← YOU ARE HERE   │
│ └─ Settings                    │
├─ Footer (Connection Status)    │
└────────────────────────────────┘
    ↓
┌─ SidebarInset ─────────────────┐
│ ReadOnlyBanner (if static mode)│
│ ┌─ Main Content ─────────────┐ │
│ │ Page-specific content here │ │
│ └─────────────────────────────┘ │
└────────────────────────────────┘

Mobile: Sidebar hidden, bottom nav shows
```

**Responsive Breakpoints:**
- Mobile: Single column, bottom navigation, full-width content
- Tablet+ (≥768px): Sidebar visible, content inset
- Desktop+ (≥1024px): Detail panels open as slide-overs

---

### API ENDPOINTS & STATIC DATA INTEGRATION

**Workflow API Endpoints (from spec ac-17):**
```
GET /api/meta/workflows
  → Returns list of workflow definitions
  → Includes: id, name, description, steps, triggers, loop_variants
  → Accessible in both daemon and static modes
```

**Static Mode Support:**
- Workflows data embedded in `kspec-snapshot.json` export
- Fallback function: `fetchWorkflowsStatic(params?)` 
- Pattern: Check `isStaticMode()`, route to static or daemon API
- Write operations (Start workflow) disabled in static mode with tooltip

**WebSocket Topics:**
- `workflows:updates` — Subscribe for real-time workflow definition changes
- `agents` — Subscribe for agent invocation status (if workflows trigger agents)

---

### EXISTING IMPLEMENTATION PATTERNS TO FOLLOW

**Plan Page (Reference Implementation):**
- Status filter dropdown (draft/approved/active/completed/rejected)
- Card-based grid layout (1 col mobile, 2 col tablet, 3 col+ desktop)
- Badge chips for status with color mapping
- Icon indicators (MapIcon, FileTextIcon, ListTodoIcon)
- Progress metrics displayed
- Empty state with icon + help text

**Agent Page (Reference Implementation):**
- Dispatch engine status section (running/stopped toggle)
- Active invocations list with real-time updates
- Agent definition cards in responsive grid
- Completed invocation counts incremented by WebSocket
- Live regions for screen reader announcements
- Loading skeleton matching content structure

**Navigation Pattern (Sidebar.svelte):**
```typescript
type NavItem = { path: string; label: string; icon: typeof IconComponent; badgeKey?: 'inbox' | 'observations' | 'pendingReview' };
type NavGroup = { label: string; items: NavItem[] };

// Render with SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuButton
// Active route highlighted via $page.url.pathname matching
```

---

### KEY ARCHITECTURAL DECISIONS

1. **Library-First Design**: Core is @kynetic-ai/shared types library; web-ui consumes via imports
2. **Mode-Aware Code**: Every data fetch checks `isStaticMode()` for graceful degradation
3. **Append-Only Updates**: Task notes, observations use supersession (never delete, mark superseded)
4. **Reactive Derivation**: Use `$derived` for computed state (filtered lists, counts, status summaries)
5. **WebSocket Opt-In**: Static mode skips WebSocket entirely; no errors in browser console
6. **Project Isolation**: X-Kspec-Dir header ensures multi-project data separation
7. **Accessible**: Live regions, semantic HTML, contrast-compliant colors, keyboard navigation

---

### TESTING PATTERNS OBSERVED

**E2E (Playwright):**
- Ephemeral ports for daemon isolation
- Isolated HOME/config to prevent test interference
- Data attributes for element selection: `data-testid="workflows-loading"`
- Fixtures handle daemon lifecycle setup/teardown

**Component Structure:**
- No direct file writes in components
- API errors caught and displayed in alert banners
- Empty states prevent errors when data is missing

---

### SUMMARY

The workflows page should:
- **Fetch** workflows from `/api/meta/workflows` (with static fallback)
- **Display** workflow cards showing: id/name, description, ordered steps, trigger type, loop variant
- **Style** using status badges (color-coded), card grid layout (responsive columns)
- **Enable** "Start Workflow" button that POSTs to daemon API
- **Update** in real-time via WebSocket topic `workflows:updates`
- **Degrade** gracefully in static mode (disable write actions, use embedded JSON)
- **Integrate** into Config sidebar group with Workflow icon
- **Follow** component patterns: title, error alert, loading skeleton, empty state, main content

All code should include AC annotations linking to spec items, match the Svelte 5 runes pattern, use shadcn-svelte components, and respect the design token system for colors and spacing.

  - _ulid: 01KF782ZSH8JG4CCJRWVQQ9G5R
    id: spec-first
    trigger: behavior-change
    description: |
      Check spec coverage before implementing changes.

      update the spec first.
    steps:
      - type: check
        content: Does the spec cover this change?
        on_fail: Update or create spec before proceeding
      - type: decision
        content: What is the spec status?
        options:
          - Spec exists and matches -> Derive task, proceed
          - Spec exists but outdated -> Update spec first
          - No spec exists -> Create spec first (behavior) or task directly (infra)
      - type: action
        content: Update or create spec item if needed
      - type: action
        content: Derive task from spec via kspec derive @spec-item
      - type: action
        content: Implement the change
  - _ulid: 01KF782ZSH103A99NV1VY65CFB
    id: session-start
    trigger: session-start
    description: |
      Get context at the beginning of a work session.
    steps:
      - type: action
        content: Run kspec session start to get context
      - type: check
        content: Are there active (in_progress) tasks?
        on_fail: Pick from ready tasks or triage inbox
      - type: action
        content: Review ready tasks and inbox items
      - type: action
        content: Start work on chosen task via kspec task start
  - _ulid: 01KF782ZSJH58GHDTHC873XJMA
    id: task-lifecycle
    trigger: task-complete
    description: |
      Complete a task properly with notes and cleanup.
    steps:
      - type: action
        content: Add completion note describing what was done
      - type: action
        content: Run kspec task complete @task --reason "summary"
      - type: check
        content: Are there uncommitted changes?
        on_fail: Commit changes with descriptive message
      - type: action
        content: Review if task unblocked other work
  - _ulid: 01KF782ZSJYAF3XCN89YD44XYM
    id: inbox-triage
    trigger: session-start
    description: |
      Triage inbox items during session context review.
    steps:
      - type: action
        content: Review oldest inbox items first
      - type: decision
        content: For each item, ask these questions
        options:
          - Still relevant? No -> delete
          - Scope clear? Yes -> promote to task
          - Needs spec work? -> Create/update spec first
          - Still unclear? -> Leave, add tag, revisit later
      - type: check
        content: Has item survived 3+ triage sessions?
        on_fail: Either promote with clear scope or delete
  - _ulid: 01KFBQCCJFBAAT6JAP5KYTKRHV
    id: codebase-audit
    trigger: pre-release
    description: "Comprehensive codebase audit for release readiness. Five-phase workflow: parallel
      exploration (docs, code, config, tests, specs), compilation by severity, interactive triage,
      execution, and summary."
    steps: []
  - _ulid: 01KFKS5NT2T98M70QQ4FZB2VTW
    id: session-reflect
    trigger: session-end
    description: Structured reflection after work sessions. Surfaces learnings, identifies friction, and
      captures improvements for system evolution.
    steps:
      - type: action
        content: |
          Identify what worked well this session.
          Be specific: "categorizing items first" not "good planning".
          Consider: workflows, tools/commands, communication, decisions.
      - type: action
        content: |
          Identify friction points - where things were harder than needed.
          Focus on systemic issues, not one-off mistakes.
          Consider: repetitive steps, missing commands, context loss, workarounds.
      - type: action
        content: |
          Check if friction points are already tracked.
          Search specs, tasks, AND inbox before proposing new improvements.
          For each: note if already tracked, partially covered, or untracked.
        exit_criteria:
          - Searched specs for relevant features
          - Searched tasks for existing work
          - Searched inbox for captured ideas
      - type: action
        content: |
          For untracked friction, propose concrete improvements.
          Include: what it would do, how it helps, rough scope (small/medium/large).
      - type: decision
        content: Present findings to user - ask about each improvement one at a time
        options:
          - Worth capturing -> proceed to capture
          - Needs refinement -> discuss and refine
          - Not worth it -> skip and continue
          - Done with reflection -> complete workflow
      - type: action
        content: |
          Capture approved items using appropriate destination:
          - Actionable improvements: kspec inbox add "..." --tag reflection
          - Friction patterns: kspec meta observe friction "..."
